extracted.intended_audience: attorneys registered to practice before the USPTO (patent practitioners) and Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, procedures, and sanctions governing resolution of a USPTO disciplinary complaint via a Proposed Settlement Agreement and Final Order, including required stipulations, misconduct definitions, remedial measures, publication, and enforcement mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction and authority to approve settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction and authority to approve proposed settlement agreements pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed Settlement Agreements resolving disciplinary complaints must be submitted for approval to the Under Secretary of Commerce for Intellectual Property and Director of the USPTO (or designee) and must satisfy the applicable statutes and regulations cited above.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 — requirements for settlement agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: A Proposed Settlement Agreement must set forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed-upon sanctions and satisfy the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the § 11.26 requirements are met, the Proposed Settlement Agreement resolves all disciplinary action by the USPTO arising from the stipulated facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance of separate client trust (Coltaf) and operating accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must maintain a client trust account (Coltaf) for client funds and a separate operating account for business/operating transactions of the law practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper separation of funds is required to avoid commingling and related misconduct; failures in account management that cause dishonored payments can be sanctionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper handling of electronic funds transfers (EFTs) for USPTO fees
rubrics_metrics.description: EFTs for USPTO fees must be drawn from an appropriate account with sufficient funds and staff must be trained in proper EFT procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing staff to submit EFTs from frozen or insufficient accounts leading to dishonored transfers is improper; establishing EFT capability on the correct trust account and training staff are mitigating remedial steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misrepresentation — 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct involving misrepresentation, exemplified here by submitting EFTs to the USPTO that were dishonored for insufficient funds, violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of dishonored payments to the USPTO may be treated as misrepresentation and subject to discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct reflecting adversely on fitness to practice — 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct that adversely reflects on a practitioner's fitness to practice law — such as failing to adequately supervise staff and permitting submission of dishonored EFTs — violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervisory failures that result in misconduct by staff can be independent bases for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions structure: suspension, stayed suspension, and probation
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanctions may include suspension from practice before the USPTO (here: 24 months), which can be stayed, and imposition of a probationary period (here: 24 months) during which the practitioner may continue to practice unless the stay is lifted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stayed suspension allows continued practice during probation unless the OED Director and USPTO Director lift the stay following enforcement procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial continuing legal education (CLE) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must enroll in and complete a three-hour continuing legal education class(es) approved by the Colorado Bar Association on law office management for the solo and small practitioner that includes specific information on financial bookkeeping and ethics within 90 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must, within 120 days, provide the OED Director an affidavit attesting to enrollment and completion along with corroborating documentation (e.g., CLE credit evidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restitution and payment of dishonored fees
rubrics_metrics.description: After notice that EFTs were dishonored, Respondent paid the USPTO fees corresponding to the dishonored EFTs and offered to pay fees arising from the untimely payment from Respondent's deposit account at the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making good on dishonored transfers and offering to cover untimely-payment-related fees are expected remedial actions and can be relevant to settlement terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigation steps required or credited (training, audit, EFT capability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitigating corrective actions include training staff in proper EFT procedures, conducting an audit of client accounts related to the dishonored EFTs, and establishing EFT capability for the Coltaf trust account at the new bank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documented corrective steps are cited in the Final Order and can influence the sanctioning outcome (e.g., stay of suspension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause and enforcement procedure for probation violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes the respondent failed to comply with the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule during probation, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to respondent at last address of record, and grant 15 days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the 15-day response period and consideration of any response, if noncompliance is still believed, the OED Director will forward the Order to Show Cause, respondent's response, and evidence to the USPTO Director and request lifting the stay and immediate suspension for up to the original suspension period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences if suspension is imposed (procedural and administrative actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the stay of the suspension is lifted and the respondent is suspended: the respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; the OED Director shall disseminate information in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59; the USPTO shall dissociate respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates; respondent may not use or obtain USPTO customer numbers or PKI certificates until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate administrative actions accompany suspension to prevent continued access/representation before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and redaction requirements for Final Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room, except that application numbers and the names of persons other than the respondent shall be redacted; the OED Director shall publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public discipline notices are published but sensitive third-party identifiers must be redacted as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director must give notice of the public discipline and reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where respondent is admitted, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order triggers statutorily-required notifications to other jurisdictions and public disclosure channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of the disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, shall be considered when addressing further complaints or evidence of the same or similar misconduct and/or in any future disciplinary proceeding as an aggravating factor and/or to rebut statements made on respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior settlements and orders can be used both as aggravation and as evidentiary rebuttal in future disciplinary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement here specifies each party bears its own costs; other settlements may allocate costs differently.
